# Greg's Crowd-Pleaser Baked Chicken & Rice 🏠

::: {.dish-meta}
**Region:** The author's kitchen (California, USA)  ·  **Family:** One-dish oven bake
**Serves:** 6–8  ·  **Active time:** 25 minutes  ·  **Total:** 1 hour 30 min
**Assembly:** 🍲 Cooked together — browned chicken baked right on top of the rice
:::

Every cook needs one dish they can make on autopilot for a hungry crowd, and this
is mine. Season and brown some chicken, tip rice and broth into a baking dish,
lay the chicken on top, and let the oven do the rest. It's forgiving, it scales,
it works with whatever chicken you've got, and it pleases a table full of
different eaters. Naturally gluten-free and dairy-free, too.

## Why this one

I reach for this whenever there are more people than time: a full house, a potluck,
a weeknight that got away from me. It has three things going for it.

- **It's flexible.** Any chicken cuts work — but it's best with a quartered bird or
  any **bone-in, skin-on** pieces, which brown well and stay juicy through the bake.
- **It's hands-off.** Once it's in the oven it needs nothing until the lid comes off.
- **It feeds everyone.** Mild enough for kids, savory enough for adults, and a
  clean plate for gluten-free and dairy-free guests without a second thought.

The one principle that makes it work: the rice cooks in seasoned broth *under* the
chicken, so it drinks up all the rendered fat and spice dripping down from above.

## Ingredients

**Chicken**

- A quartered chicken, or ~1.5 kg (3–3.5 lb) bone-in, skin-on pieces (thighs,
  drumsticks, quarters — mix as you like)
- Salt and black pepper
- 1–2 tsp ground cumin
- 1–2 tsp chili powder
- 1–2 tbsp neutral oil, for browning

**Rice & broth**

- 2 cups (about 370 g) long-grain white rice
- 4 cups (about 950 ml) broth — **vegetable or chicken broth beats water** (but
  water works in a pinch)
- Aromatics: 1 onion, diced; 3–4 cloves garlic, minced; and any of a diced bell
  pepper, a bay leaf or two, a little more cumin — whatever you have
- Salt, to season the rice layer

**To serve:** a big green salad

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Gluten-free · dairy-free:** naturally both — chicken, rice, broth, and spices.
Just use a **gluten-free, dairy-free broth**, and check that your chili powder
blend is gluten-free (most are). No butter, no cream, no flour anywhere.
:::

## Method

1. **Heat the oven to 350 °F (175 °C).**
2. **Season and brown the chicken.** Pat the pieces dry and season all over with
   salt, pepper, cumin, and chili powder. Heat the oil in a large skillet over
   medium-high and brown the chicken well on all sides — you're after color and
   rendered fat, not cooking it through. Set aside.
3. **Build the rice layer.** Scatter the rice and aromatics evenly across a large
   baking dish (a lasagna dish is perfect). Season with a little salt.
4. **Add the broth.** Pour in the broth — **about twice the volume of the rice**
   (roughly 4 cups for 2 cups of rice). Stir gently so the rice settles into an
   even layer. Tip in any juices and browned bits from the skillet for extra
   flavor.
5. **Top with the chicken.** Lay the browned chicken pieces on top of the rice,
   skin-side up, so their fat bastes the rice as it bakes.
6. **Bake covered.** Cover tightly (a lid or foil) and bake **45 minutes**.
7. **Uncover and finish.** Remove the cover and bake another **15–20 minutes** at
   the same temperature, to dry the rice slightly and crisp the chicken skin.
8. **Check and adjust.** The chicken is done at **165 °F (74 °C)** at the bone, and
   the rice should be tender with the liquid absorbed. Want more color on top? Give
   it a few minutes under the broiler. Rice still a little wet? Uncover and bake a
   few minutes more. Too dry? Add a splash of hot broth and re-cover to steam.
9. **Serve** straight from the dish, with a big green salad alongside.

## Make it yours

- **Any cuts, any crowd.** Boneless pieces work but cook faster — check them early.
  To feed more, scale the rice and broth (keep the 1:2 ratio) and use a bigger dish;
  add 10–15 minutes to the covered bake for a deeper pan.
- **Change the accent.** Swap the cumin-and-chili for smoked paprika and thyme, or a
  curry powder, or a lemon-and-oregano lean — the method stays identical.
- **Sneak in vegetables.** Scatter carrots, peas, or chopped greens into the rice
  layer so it's a complete one-dish meal.
- **Broth is the upgrade.** If you do one thing, use a good stock instead of water —
  it's the difference between fine and can't-stop-eating-it.
